subject: Renewal capacity planning - FinWave (ensemble commit redesign)
messages:
From: Lara Mendez <lara@finwave.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel@finwave.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — committed capacity flexibility

Hey Aditya,

We’re starting the renewal conversation for our Dedicated pool (contract FW-2025-NA). Usage in Q2 looked spikier than expected — spikes during trading hours, but lower baseline overnight. Procurement wants to avoid a step-up that overspends, while our engineering team wants some assurance they can scale quickly during market events.

Questions: can Redwood offer a commit that maps to an "active slab + burst" model instead of a single fixed tranche? And can we get visibility into real utilization buckets so we can align the committed amount to actual steady-state rather than peak?

I attached the Q2 usage export. Can we get a proposal before our internal renewal review (end of month)?

Thanks,
Lara
Head of Platform — FinWave AI

Attachment: FW_usage_report_Q2_2027.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Mendez <lara@finwave.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — committed capacity flexibility

Hi Lara — thanks for the export, that was helpful. Quick read-through notes in-line, and high level proposal below.

Proposal (summary):
- Adaptive slab commitment: convert your single tranche into two components: a guaranteed steady slab (40 GPUs baseline) + a flexible burst slab (up to 80 GPUs) billed on usage above baseline at a discounted overage rate.
- Smoothing buffer: maintain a 10% warm pool to reduce spin-up latency for burst requests (pre-warmed instances that can be reclaimed by other customers if unused).
- Utilization mapping: we’ll provide a 7-day rolling utilization fingerprint and a heatmap by hour so you can pick the baseline slab that matches 60–70th percentile sustained load.
- Contract mechanics: a 12-month amendment that converts current commit to the above: baseline monthly minimum + metered burst with a capped monthly overage for predictability.

Preliminary numbers (based on your Q2 export):
- Observed 90th percentile concurrent GPU equivalents: ~62
- Recommended baseline slab: 40 GPUs (covers ~65% of active hours)
- Estimated monthly cost delta vs. full 80-GPU commit: ~-18% (you’d pay less on average, with controlled burst pricing)

Attachments: adaptive_slab_proposal_v2.pdf (sketch + cost model). Vivek, Soojin — can you validate the latency impact for 10% warm pool and confirm the warm-pool reclaim policy?

Next steps:
1) We iterate the cost model and SLA amendment (I’ve attached a draft).
2) Legal writes amendment; we provide a DocuSign-ready packet.
3) Ops runbook: warm pool lifecycle and SLA for warm pool reclaim.

Will follow up with updated numbers tomorrow.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-1243

Attachments: adaptive_slab_proposal_v2.pdf, sla_amendment_draft.docx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — committed capacity flexibility

Aditya — quick notes from infra:
- 10% warm pool (for 40 baseline) = 4 GPUs reserved as pre-warmed. Latency improvement for first-token on burst loads: ~400–700ms depending on model.
- Warm pool reclaim policy: we can mark those nodes as soft-preemptible after 5 minutes of idle; reclaim is controlled via integration with your job priority tags so FinWave workloads retain priority during trading windows.
- Cost estimate update: baseline 40 GPUs (V100 equiv) priced at baseline commit; burst at 0.65x of list on metered usage; warm pool charged at 0.15x baseline for reservation overhead.

I’ll add a micro-benchmark for your trading model and include it in the drive link by EOD.

-Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — committed capacity flexibility

Lara — attaching the micro-benchmark and updated cost table. Key changes after infra input:
- Expected 95th p99 tail latency remains within your SLO for the models you flagged when using a 10% warm pool.
- New blended cost delta: -12% vs. full-fixed 80-GPU commit after accounting for warm-pool reservation fees.

Open questions for FinWave:
- Which trading hours do you want priority access for warm-pool reclaim? (we suggest 09:30–16:00 ET)
- Do you want nightly autoscale windows extended by 2 hours to allow model warmers to pre-cache KV caches?

If you confirm priority windows, we’ll bake them into the SLA amendment and send a DocuSign-ready set.

Thanks — hoping we can close this week for your end-of-month review.

Best,
Aditya

Attachment: infra_microbenchmark_results.pdf
